2031.text: Assertion : No taste sensation is evoked when drop of distilled water is put on human tongue.Reason : Man does not possess taste buds for tasting water.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
2031.sol: No taste sensation is evoked when distilled water is put on human tongue because man does not possess taste buds for tasting water. The taste buds present on the tongue send nerve impulses to the brain which actually preceives the taste sensation. Some mammals such as rhesus monkeys, pigs, cats and dogs possess some taste buds which send nerve impulses to the brain when distilled water is applied on them. It seems, therefore, that water may stimulate these taste buds to evoke taste sensation in these animals.

5168.text: What is the depression of freezing point, when mole fraction of non-electrolyte solute in aqueous solution is $0.01 ?\left(\mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{f}}\right.$ of $\left.\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=1.86 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$
5168.sol:
$\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{ m}_1} \times \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}$ We have, $\mathrm{x}_2=\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_1+\mathrm{n}_2} \approx \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_1}=0.01$
Taking $1 \mathrm{ L}$ of water, mass of water $=1 \mathrm{ kg}=1000 \mathrm{ g}
\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)=\mathrm{n}_{1}=\frac{1000 \mathrm{ g}}{18 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}}=55.55 \mathrm{ mol}\\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}_{2}=55.55 \times0.01=0.556 \mathrm{ mol}\\
& \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\ mathrm{f}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{ m}_1} \times \mathrm{K}_{\ mathrm{f}}=\frac{0.556 \mathrm{ mol}}{1 \mathrm{ kg}} \times1.86 \\
& =1.034 \mathrm{ K} \approx1.043 \mathrm{ K}
\end{aligned}$

y & =(-2)^3-3(-2)=-2 \\
\therefore \quad Q & =(-2,-2)
\end{aligned}

Equation$ of Normal isy-y_1=m   $\left(x-x_1\right) \begin{aligned}$y+2 & $=\frac{-1}{9}($x+2) \\
x+9 y & =-20

Required Equation$ of normal isx+9 y= \pm20$ Hence, option (3) is correct.

7065.text: The length of the transverse common tangent of the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x + 4y + 4 = 0$ and $x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x - 2y + 1 = 0$ is
7065.sol:
Let,

${C}_{1} ≡ x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x + 4y + 4 = 0$

Centre, ${c}_{2} ≡ \left(1, - 2\right)$ and radius& ${r}_{1} = 1$

${C}_{2} ≡ x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x - 2y + 1 = 0$

Centre, ${c}_{1} ≡ \left(-2, 1\right)$ and radius& ${r}_{2} = 2$

Now, distance between centres is given by

${c}_{1}{c}_{2} = \sqrt{\left(- 2 - 1\right)2 + \left(1 + 2\right)2} = \sqrt{18}$

Now, we know that the length of transverse common tangent is given by

$\sqrt{\left({c}_{1}{c}_{2}\right)2 - \left({r}_{1} + {r}_{2}\right)2}$

$= \sqrt{18 - \left(1 + 2\right)2} =3$.

10214.text:
For the parabola $y^{2} + 6y - 2x + 5 = 0,$ match the items in List-$I$ with the suitable item in List-$II$ given below:
List-$I$ List-$II$
$\left(I\right)$ Vertex $\left(A\right)$ $\left(- \dfrac{3}{2}, - 3\right)$
$\left(II\right)$ Focus $\left(B\right)$ $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, - 3\right)$
$\left(III\right)$ Equation of the directrix $\left(C\right)$ $2x + 5 = 0$
$\left(IV\right)$ Equation of the axis $\left(D\right)$ $2x + y + 3 = 0$
~ & $\left(E\right)$ $y + 3 = 0$
~ & $\left(F\right)$ $\left(- 2, - 3\right)$

The correct matching is
10214.sol:
Given:

$y^{2} + 6y - 2x + 5 = 0$

$⇒ \left(y + 3\right)2 = 2x + 4$

$⇒ \left(y + 3\right)2 = 2\left(x + 2\right)$

The form: $\left(y - k\right)2 = 4a \left($ x - h\right)$, where, the vertex is& $V $\left(h, k\right)$

Therefore,

Vertex $≡ \left(-2, - 3\right)$

Now, $4a = 2 ⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now, we know that focus lies at a distance $a$ from the vertex of the parabola.

Therefore,

$- 2 + a = - 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

So, coordinates of focus are $\left(\dfrac{- 3}{2}, -3\right)$

Equation of directrix in standard form is $x + a = 0$ from the vertex.

Therefore,& equation of directrix is&

$x = - 2 - \dfrac{1}{2} = - \dfrac{5}{2}$

or $2x + 5 = 0$

And, axes is $y = - 3\text{or}y + 3 = 0$.

10265.text: If the normal to the parabola $y^2=4 x$ at $P(1,2)$ meets the parabola again in $Q$, then coordinates of $Q$ are
10265.sol:
The given equation of the parabola is
$y^2=4 x$
Equation of tangent at $(1,2)$ is
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & y \cdot 2 & =2(x+1) \\ \Rightarrow & & y & =x+1\end{aligned}$
Slope of tangent $=1\therefore$ slope of the normal $=-1$
Equation of the normal passing through $(1,2)$ is
$\begin{aligned} & y-2=-1(x-1) \\ & y-2=-x+1 \Rightarrow x+y=3\end{aligned}$
This equation again meet at $Q$ of the parabola, then
$\begin{array}{cc} & y^2=4(3-y) \\ \Rightarrow & y^2=12-4 y \Rightarrow y^2+4 y-12=0 \\ \Rightarrow & (y-2)(y+6)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & y=2,6\end{array}
If $y=-6$, then $x=3-(-6)=9\therefore$ The coordinates of point $Q$ are $(9,-6)$.$

11384.text: If $a$ is a positive integer such that the roots of the equation $7x^{2} - 13x + a = 0$ are rational numbers, then the smallest possible value of $a$& is
11384.sol:
Given, $7x^{2} - 13x + a = 0$

For rational roots $D \ge 0$ and $D$ must be perfect square.

$⇒ 169 - 28a \ge 0$

Now, we see from options that $a = 7 \text{ and } a = 8$ are not possible as then $D < 0$.

For $a = 5$, $D = 168 - 28 \times 5 = 29 \ge 0$ But it is not perfect square.

For $a = 6$, $D = 169 - 28 \times 6 = 1 \ge 0$ and it is a perfect square.

Hence, the smallest possible value of $a$ is $6$.

11966.text: Starting from the point $A  \left(-3, 4\right)$, a moving object touches $2x + y - 7 = 0$ at $B$ and reaches the point $C  \left(0, 1\right)$. If the object travels along the shortest path, the distance between $A$ and $B$ is
11966.sol:
Given,

Point& $A \left(-3, 4\right)$ and& $C \left(0, 1\right)$ and let moving point be& $B \left(x, y\right)$

Now given equation of line $2x + y = 7 ⇒ y = - 2x + 7 . . . \left(1\right)$

Now finding distance we get, $AB + BC = \sqrt{\left(x + 3\right)2 + \left($ y - 4\right)2}$ + \sqrt{ \left($ x - 0\right)2 + $\left($ y - 1\right)2} . . . $\left(2\right)$

Now substituting the value of $y$ in& (2) we get,

$= \sqrt{\left(x + 3\right)2 + \left(- 2x + 7 - 4\right)2} + \sqrt{\left(x - 0\right)2 + \left(- 2x + 7 - 1\right)2}$

$= \sqrt{x^{2} + 9 + 6x + 4x^{2} + 9 - 12x} + \sqrt{x^{2} + 4x^{3} + 36 - 24x}$

$= \sqrt{5x^{2} - 6x + 18} + \sqrt{5x^{2} - 24x + 36}$

Now let $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{5x^{2} - 6x + 18} + \sqrt{5x^{2} - 24x + 36}$

Now to get minimum value we will differentiate wrt $x$ we get,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{10x - 6}{2\sqrt{5x^{2} - 6x + 18}} + \dfrac{10x - 24}{2\sqrt{5x^{2} - 24x + 36}}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{5x - 3}{5x^{2} - 6x + 18} + \dfrac{5x - 12}{5x^{2} - 24x + 36} =0$

$⇒ \dfrac{5x - 3}{5x^{2} - 6x + 18} = \dfrac{12 - 5x}{5x^{2} - 24x + 36}$

Now squaring on bothisdes we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(5x - 3\right)2}{5x^{2} - 6x + 18} = \dfrac{\left(12 - 5x\right)2}{5x^{3} - 24x + 36}$

$⇒ \dfrac{25x^{2} + 9 - 30x}{5x^{2} - 6x + 18} = \dfrac{144 + 25x^{2} - 120x}{5x^{2} - 24x + 36}$

By solving the above equation we get $25x^{2} - 192x + 252 = 0$

As it is a quadratic equation, we get two values of $x$.

So, $x = \dfrac{+ 192 \pm \sqrt{\left(192\right)2 - 4\left(252\right)\left(25\right)}}{2\left(25\right)}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{192 \pm \sqrt{11664}}{50}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{192 \pm 108}{50}$

So, $x = \dfrac{192 + 108}{50}\text{or}\dfrac{192 - 108}{50}$

$⇒ x = 6\text{or}\dfrac{42}{25}$

So we will take $x = \dfrac{42}{25}$ as it is a smaller value and& we want minimum distance,

Then by substitute $x$ in the equation we get $y = \dfrac{91}{25}$

So, $B \left(x, y\right) = \left(\dfrac{42}{25}, \dfrac{91}{25}\right)

Now by distance formula we get $AB = $\dfrac{9\sqrt{170}}{25}$

Let the equation of line passing through origin is $y=m x$ which cut the parallel lines $x-y+10=0 and x-y+20=0$ at points $A and B$ respectively. Then, co-ordinates of points $A and B$ are,

$\begin{gathered}$y=m x $\text{$ and }x-y+10=0 \\
x-m x=-10 \\
x=$\frac{-10}{1-m}=\frac{10}{m-1} \text{$ and }y=$\frac{10 m}{m-1}$\\
\therefore A$\left(\frac{10}{m-1}, \frac{10 m}{m-1}\right)
\end{gathered}$So,

$\begin{aligned}$O A & =$\sqrt{\frac{100}{(m-1)^2}+\frac{100 m^2}{(m-1)^2}}$\\
& =$\sqrt{\frac{100\left(1+m^2\right)}{(m-1)^2}}=\frac{10 \sqrt{\left(1+m^2\right)}}{m-1}
\end{aligned}$Similarly, coordinate of point $B$ is
$\therefore$
B$\left(\frac{20}{m-1}, \frac{20 m}{m-1}\right)$Then, $O B=\sqrt{\frac{400}{(m-1)^2}+\frac{400 m^2}{(m-1)^2}}=\frac{20 \sqrt{1+m^2}}{(m-1)}$
Let point $P(h, k)$ lies on the line $y=m x$
So,

k=m h \Rightarrow m=$\frac{k}{h}$and $\quad O P=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}$
Now, $O A, O P, O B$ in H.P.
So, $\frac{1}{O A}, \frac{1}{O P}, \frac{1}{O B}$ in AP.
Hence, $\quad \frac{1}{O P}=\frac{1}{O A}+\frac{1}{O B}\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{2}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2}}=\frac{m-1}{10 \sqrt{1+m^2}}+\frac{m-1}{20 \sqrt{1+m^2}}$\\
& $\frac{2}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2}}=\frac{m-1}{10 \sqrt{1+m^2}}\left[$1+$\frac{1}{2}\right]
\end{aligned}$Putting the value of $m$, we get

$\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{2}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2}}=\frac{\left(\frac{k}{h}-1\right)}{10 \cdot \sqrt{1+\frac{k^2}{h^2}}} \cdot \frac{3}{2}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{2}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2}}$& =$\frac{3(k-h) / h}{20 \frac{\sqrt{h^2+k^2}}{h}}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{2}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2}}=$& $\frac{3(k-h)}{20 \sqrt{h^2+k^2}}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad 3(k-h) & =40 \Rightarrow 3 h-3 k+40=0
\end{aligned}

Hence, locus of the point is

12738.text:
If $x = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left[cot \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\right]$ and $\theta \in\left(\dfrac{- \pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right), then consider$ the following statements:

I: coshx = $sec2\theta
$ II:sinhx = - $tan2\theta

Then which one$ of the following options is true?
12738.sol:
Given, $x = {\log}_{e}\left[cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\right]$

$⇒ {e}^{x} = cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)$

            $= \dfrac{cos\theta - sin\theta}{cos\theta + sin\theta}$

Now, $cos\text{h}x = \dfrac{{e}^{x} + {e}^{- x}}{2}$

             $= \left\{\dfrac{{e}^{x} + \dfrac{1}{{e}^{x}}}{2}\right\}$

            $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\dfrac{cos\theta - sin\theta}{cos\theta + sin\theta} + \dfrac{cos\theta + sin\theta}{cos\theta - sin\theta}\right\}$

            $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\dfrac{{\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)}^{2} + {\left(cos\theta + sin\theta\right)}^{2}}{\left(cos\theta + sin\theta\right)\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)}\right\}$

             $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\dfrac{2}{\left({cos}^{2}\theta - {sin}^{2}\theta\right)}\right\}$

              $= \left\{\dfrac{1}{cos2\theta}\right\}$

               $= sec2\theta$

And, $sin\text{h}x = \dfrac{{e}^{x} - {e}^{- x}}{2}$

            $= \left\{\dfrac{{e}^{x} - \dfrac{1}{{e}^{x}}}{2}\right\}$

             $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\dfrac{cos\theta - sin\theta}{cos\theta + sin\theta} - \dfrac{cos\theta + sin\theta}{cos\theta - sin\theta}\right\}$

               $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\dfrac{{\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)}^{2} - {\left(cos\theta + sin\theta\right)}^{2}}{\left(cos\theta + sin\theta\right)\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)}\right\}$

              $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\dfrac{- 4cos\thetasin\theta}{\left({cos}^{2}\theta - {sin}^{2}\theta\right)}\right\}$

              $= \left\{\dfrac{- 2cos\thetasin\theta}{cos2\theta}\right\}$

 $= - \left\{\dfrac{sin2\theta}{cos2\theta}\right\}$

$= - tan2\theta$

20171.subject: Chemistry
20171.text: The Molar conductivity of $0.05 \mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{MgCl}_2$ is $194.5 \mathrm{ ohm}^{-1} \mathrm{ cm}^2$ per mole at room temperature. A Conductivity cell with electrodes having $3.0 \mathrm{ cm}^2$ surface area and $1.0 \mathrm{ cm}$ apart is filled with the solution of $\mathrm{MgCl}_2$. What would be the resistance offered by the conductivity cell?
20171.sol:
The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is related to the conductivity $\kappa$ and molarity $C$ by the formula $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1000 \times \kappa}{C}$.

Given $\Lambda_m = 194.5 \text{ ohm}^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $C = 0.05 \text{ M}$, we calculate the conductivity $\kappa$ as follows:

$\kappa = \dfrac{\Lambda_m \times C}{1000} = \dfrac{194.5 \times 0.05}{1000} = \dfrac{9.725}{1000} = 0.009725 \text{ S cm}^{-1}$.

The cell constant $G^{*}$ is defined as $\dfrac{l}{A}$, where $l$ is the distance between electrodes and $A$ is the surface area of the electrodes.

$G^{*} = \dfrac{1.0 \text{ cm}}{3.0 \text{ cm}^2} = 0.3333 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The relationship between conductivity $\kappa$, resistance $R$, and cell constant $G^{*}$ is $\kappa = \dfrac{G^{*}}{R}$.

Rearranging for resistance $R$:

$R = \dfrac{G^{*}}{\kappa} = \dfrac{0.3333}{0.009725} \approx 34.27 \text{ ohms}$.

Answer: 34.27 ohms

20215.text: Identify the correct structure of o-ethyl anisole.
20215.sol:
Anisole is the common name for methoxybenzene, which consists of a benzene ring attached to a methoxy group ($-OCH_3$).

The prefix 'o-' (ortho) indicates that an ethyl group ($-C_2H_5$) is attached to the adjacent carbon atom (position 2) on the benzene ring relative to the methoxy group.

Therefore, o-ethyl anisole has an $-OCH_3$ group and a $-C_2H_5$ group at the 1 and 2 positions of the benzene ring. This structure corresponds to option (D).

20372.subject: Chemistry
20372.text: The product formed in the following reaction is:
20372.sol:
The given reaction is the addition of HBr to an alkene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. This proceeds via a free-radical mechanism (Kharasch effect or anti-Markovnikov addition).

First, the peroxide initiates the reaction to generate a bromine radical (Br^{\bullet}$).

The $Br^{\bullet}$ radical attacks the double bond to form the most stable carbon radical intermediate. There are two possible sites for the attack on the $HO-C_6H_4-CH=CH-CH_3$ molecule:
1. Attack at the \alpha$-carbon gives a secondary alkyl radical: $HO-C_6H_4-CH(Br)-\dot{C}H-CH_3$
2. Attack at the $\beta$-carbon gives a benzylic radical: $HO-C_6H_4-\dot{C}H-CH(Br)-CH_3$

The benzylic radical is significantly more stable due to resonance delocalization with the benzene ring (further enhanced by the electron-donating $-OH$ group). Therefore, the $Br^{\bullet}$ radical preferentially adds to the $\beta$-carbon.

The stable benzylic radical then abstracts a hydrogen atom from another HBr molecule to yield the final product:
$HO-C_6H_4-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3$

Note that the phenolic $-OH$ group does not react with HBr because the aryl $C-O$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance and is difficult to break.

Comparing this with the given options, the correct structure is represented in option (C).

21661.sol: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } L=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x^2-2 x+1}{x^2-4 x+2}\right)^{2 x} \\ & \Rightarrow \ln L=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left[2 x \ln \left(\frac{x^2-2 x+1}{x^2-4 x+2}\right)\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \ln L=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left[2 x \ln \left(1+\frac{2 x-1}{x^2-4 x+2}\right)\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \ln L=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left[2 x\left(\frac{2 x-1}{x^2-4 x+2}-\frac{\left(\frac{2 x-1}{x^2-4 x+2}\right)^2}{2}+\right.\right. \\ & \left.+\frac{\left(\frac{2 x-1}{x^2-4 x+2}\right)^3}{3}\right) \ldots .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \ln L=\left(\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2 x(2 x-1)}{x^2-4 x+2}\right)-0+0 . \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \ln L=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{4 x^2\left(1-\frac{1}{2 x}\right)}{x^2\left(1-\frac{4}{x}+\frac{2}{x}\right)} \\ & \quad \ln L=\frac{4(1-0)}{(1-0+0)} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \ln L=4 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad L=e^4\end{aligned}$

21969.text: If a quadratic function in $x$ has the value 19 when $x=1$ and has a maximum value 20 when $x=2$, then the function is
21969.sol:
Let the quadratic function be $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$.

Since the function has a maximum value at $x=2$, the coefficient $a$ must be negative, and the vertex is at $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = 2$, which implies $b = -4a$.

The maximum value is $f(2) = a(2)^2 + b(2) + c = 4a + 2b + c = 20$.

Substituting $b = -4a$ into the equation for the maximum value: $4a + 2(-4a) + c = 20 \Rightarrow -4a + c = 20 \Rightarrow c = 20 + 4a$.

Given $f(1) = 19$, we have $a(1)^2 + b(1) + c = 19 \Rightarrow a + b + c = 19$.

Substituting $b = -4a$ and $c = 20 + 4a$ into this equation: $a - 4a + 20 + 4a = 19 \Rightarrow a + 20 = 19 \Rightarrow a = -1$.

Now find $b$ and $c$: $b = -4(-1) = 4$ and $c = 20 + 4(-1) = 16$.

The function is $f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 16$.

Answer: $f(x)=-x^2+4 x+16$

22136.subject: Mathematics
22136.text: If 2 and 3 are intercepts of a line $L=0$, then the distance of $L \equiv 0$ from the origin is
22136.sol:
The intercept form of a line with x-intercept $a$ and y-intercept $b$ is given by $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1$.

Given $a = 2$ and $b = 3$, the equation of the line is $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{3} = 1$.

Multiplying by 6, we get $3x + 2y = 6$, or $3x + 2y - 6 = 0$.

The distance $d$ of a line $Ax + By + C = 0$ from the origin $(0,0)$ is given by $d = \dfrac{|C|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}$.

Substituting $A = 3$, $B = 2$, and $C = -6$, we get $d = \dfrac{|-6|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 2^2}} = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{9 + 4}} = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{13}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{13}}$

22262.subject: Mathematics
22262.text: If $\cos A=m \cos B$ and $\cot \left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)=\lambda \tan \left(\dfrac{B-A}{2}\right), then \lambda$ is equal to
22262.sol:
Given $\cos A = m \cos B$, we have $\dfrac{\cos A}{\cos B} = m$.

Applying componendo and dividendo, $\dfrac{\cos A + \cos B}{\cos A - \cos B} = \dfrac{m+1}{m-1}$.

Using the sum-to-product formulas, $\cos A + \cos B = 2 \cos \left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right) and \cos A - \cos B = -2 \sin \left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin \left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right).

Substituting these into the ratio, \dfrac{2 \cos \left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos \left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)}{-2 \sin \left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin \left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{m+1}{m-1}.

This simplifies to $-\cot $\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \cot \left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{m+1}{m-1}.

Since $\cot $\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\tan \left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{-\tan \left(\dfrac{B-A}{2}\right)}, we have $-\cot $\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) \left( -\dfrac{1}{\tan \left(\dfrac{B-A}{2}\right)} \right) = \dfrac{m+1}{m-1}.

Therefore, $\cot $\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{m+1}{m-1} \tan \left(\dfrac{B-A}{2}\right).

Comparing this$ with the given equation\cot $\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}$\right)$ = \lambda $\tan $\left(\dfrac{B-A}{2}\right)$, we find $\lambda = \dfrac{m+1}{m-1}.

Answer: \dfrac{m+1}{m-1}$

23137.text: A hydraulic automobile lift is designed to lift cars with a maximum mass of 3000 kg. The area of cross-section of the piston carrying the board is $425 \mathrm{ cm}^2$. What maximum pressure would smaller piston have to bear?
23137.sol:
The maximum force, which the bigger piston can bear,
$F=30000 \mathrm{kgf}=3000 \times 9.8 \mathrm{ N}$
Area of piston,
$A=425 \mathrm{ cm}^2=425 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ m}^2$
$\therefore$ Maximum pressure on the bigger piston,
$p=\frac{F}{A}=\frac{300 \times 9.8}{425 \times 10^{-4}}=6.92 \times 10^4 \mathrm{ Pa}$
Since, the liquid transmits pressure equally, therefore the maximum pressure the smaller piston can bear is $6.92 \times 10^4 \mathrm{ Pa}$

23183.text: The Poisson's ratio of a material is $0.1$. If the longitudinal strain of a rod of this material is $10^{-3}$, then the percentage change in the volume of the rod will be
23183.sol:
If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the longitudinal strain and lateral strain respectively, then
$\alpha=\frac{l_{2}-l_{1}}{l_{1}}=10^{-3}=0.001$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{l_{2}}{l_{1}}=1.001$
Poisson's ratio, $\sigma=\frac{\text{ Lateral strain }}{\text{ Longitudinal strain }}$
$=\frac{\beta}{\alpha}$
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \beta=\sigma \alpha=0 \\ \text{ But, } & \beta=\frac{r_{1}-r_{2}}{r_{1}}\end{array}$
$\therefore \quad \frac{r_{1}-r_{2}}{n_{1}}=10^{-4}=0.0001$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}=0.9999$
Hence, percentage increase in vol
$=\frac{V_{2}-V_{1}}{V_{1}} \times 100$
$=\frac{\pi r_{2}^{2} l_{2}-\pi r_{1}^{2} l_{1}}{\pi r_{1}^{2} l_{1}} \times 100$
$=\left[\left(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}\right)^{2}\left(\frac{l_{2}}{l_{1}}\right)^{2}-1\right] \times 100$
$=\left[(0.9999)^{2} \times(1.0001)^{2}-1\right] \times 100$
$=0.0008 \times 100=0.08 \%$

23276.subject: Physics
23276.text:
Find the binding energy of the tritium nucleus:
[Given: mass of $1 \mathrm{H}^3=3.01605 \mathrm{ u} ; \mathrm{ m}_{\mathrm{p}}=1.00782 \mathrm{ u} ; \mathrm{ m}_{\mathrm{n}}=1.00866 \mathrm{ u}$.]
23276.sol:
The tritium nucleus $^{3}_{1}H$ consists of 1 proton and 2 neutrons.

Mass of constituents = $m_p + 2m_n = 1.00782 + 2 \times 1.00866 = 1.00782 + 2.01732 = 3.02514 \text{ u}$.

Mass defect $\Delta m = (m_p + 2m_n) - m_{nucleus} = 3.02514 - 3.01605 = 0.00909 \text{ u}$.

Binding energy = $\Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/u} = 0.00909 \times 931.5 \approx 8.467 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest given option, the binding energy is approximately 8.5 MeV.

Answer: 8.5 MeV

26172.text:
The electric field associated with an electromagnetic wave propagating in a dielectric medium is given by $\overset{\to}{E} = 30\left(2\overset{∧}{x} + \overset{∧}{y}\right)sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]V{m}^{- 1}$. Which of the following option(s) is(are) correct?

[Given: The speed of light in vacuum, $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{– 1}$]
options: The wave is polarized in the $xy$-plane with polarization angle ${30}^{o}$ with respect to the $x$-axis
The refractive index of the medium is $2$
26172.sol:
Speed of light in medium is $v = \dfrac{\omega}{k}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}\right)}{2\pi \times \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}}$

$⇒ v = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, refractive index $\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}} = 2$

$⇒ \mu = 2$

Given $\overset{\to}{E} = 30\left(2\overset{∧}{x} + \overset{∧}{y}\right)sin\left(2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right)V{m}^{- 1}$

The wave is polarised in $xy -$plane with polarisation angle $\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ with respect to $x -$axis.

Amplitude of magnetic field, ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{V} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{5}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}}$

Now, direction of $\overset{\to}{B}$ is $\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{E}\right)$

$= \overset{∧}{k} \times \dfrac{\left(2\overset{∧}{i} + \overset{∧}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{5}}$

$= \left(\dfrac{- \overset{∧}{i} + 2\overset{∧}{j}}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$.

$\overset{\to}{B} = \left(\dfrac{- \overset{∧}{i} + 2\overset{∧}{j}}{\sqrt{5}}\right) \times \dfrac{30\sqrt{5}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}}sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]Wb{m}^{- 2} = \left(- \overset{∧}{i} + 2\overset{∧}{j}\right) \times 2 \times {10}^{- 7}sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]Wb{m}^{- 2}$

Hence,

32155.subject: Chemistry
32155.text:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true ?
A. If two orbitals have the same value of $(n + l)$, the orbital with lower value of $n$ will have lower energy.
B. Energies of the orbitals in the same subshell increase with increase in atomic number.
C. The size of $2p_x$ orbital is less than the size of $3p_x$ orbital.
D. Among $5f$, $6s$, $4d$, $5p$ and $5d$ orbitals, none of the orbitals have $2$ radial nodes.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
32155.sol:
Statement A: According to the $(n+l)$ rule, if two orbitals have the same $(n+l)$ value, the orbital with the lower value of $n$ has lower energy. This statement is true.

Statement B: As the atomic number increases, the effective nuclear charge ($Z_{eff}$) increases. The energy of an orbital is proportional to $-\dfrac{Z_{eff}^2}{n^2}$. Thus, the energy becomes more negative, meaning the energy of the orbitals in the same subshell decreases with an increase in atomic number. This statement is false.

Statement C: The size of an orbital increases with an increase in the principal quantum number $n$. Therefore, the size of the $2p_x$ orbital is less than the size of the $3p_x$ orbital. This statement is true.

Statement D: The number of radial nodes is given by the formula $n - l - 1$.
For $5f$: $5 - 3 - 1 = 1$
For $6s$: $6 - 0 - 1 = 5$
For $4d$: $4 - 2 - 1 = 1$
For $5p$: $5 - 1 - 1 = 3$
For $5d$: $5 - 2 - 1 = 2$
Since the $5d$ orbital has exactly $2$ radial nodes, the statement that none of the orbitals have $2$ radial nodes is false.

Therefore, only statements A and C are true.

Answer: A and C only

33792.subject: Mathematics
33792.text: Let  $S = \left\{z \in C: \left|z - 1\right| = 1and\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - i\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) = 2\sqrt{2}\right\}$. Let ${z}_{1}, {z}_{2} \in S$ be such that  $\left|{z}_{1}\right| = \mathop{max}_{z \in s}\left|z\right|$ and $\left|{z}_{2}\right| = \mathop{min}_{z \in s}\left|z\right|$. Then ${\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2}$ equals:
33792.sol:
Given,

$\left|z - 1\right| = 1$

Now, let $z = x + iy$

$⇒ {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

And 

$\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - i\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(2x\right) - i\left(2iy\right) = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)x + y = \sqrt{2} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Solving $\left(i\right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left[\sqrt{2} - \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)x\right]}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 1 - 2x + 2 + {\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)}^{2}{x}^{2} - 2\sqrt{2}\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)x = 1$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 1 - 2x + 2 + \left(2 + 1 - 2\sqrt{2}\right){x}^{2} - 4x + 2\sqrt{2}x = 1$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 2x + 2 + 3{x}^{2} - 2{x}^{2}\sqrt{2} - 4x + 2\sqrt{2}x = 0$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 2{x}^{2}\sqrt{2} - 6x + 2\sqrt{2}x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right){x}^{2} + \left(- 6 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right){x}^{2} + \left(- 4 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)x - 2x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)x\left(x - 1\right) - 2\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(\left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)x - 2\right) = 0$

Either $x = 1$ or $x = \dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{2}} . . . \left(iii\right)$

On solving $\left(ii\right)\text{and}\left(iii\right)$ we get

For $x = 1 ⇒ y = 1 ⇒ {z}_{2} = 1 + i$ and for $x = \dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{2}} ⇒ y = \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} ⇒ {z}_{1} = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \dfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 1\right)\sqrt{2} + i - \left(1 + i\right)\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left|1 + \sqrt{2} + i - \left(1 + i\right)\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 2$

34858.text: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytan x = sin 2x$ and $y\left(0\right) = 1$, then $y\left(\pi\right)$ is equal to
34858.sol:
The given differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = sin2x$ is linear differential equation of the form

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P\left(x\right)y = Q\left(x\right)$ with $P ( x ) = tanx$, $Q ( x ) = sin2x$

Now, $I . F . = {e}^{∫ P \left(x\right)dx} = {e}^{∫ tanx dx} = {e}^{ln\left(sec x\right)} = secx$

And, the solution is $y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(x\right)\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ secxsin2xdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ \dfrac{1}{cosx}\left(2sinxcosx\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2sinxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = - 2cosx + c$

Given, $y\left(0\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 \cdot sec0 = - 2cos0 + c$

$⇒ 1 = - 2 + c$

$⇒ c = 3$

$⇒ ysec x = - 2cosx + 3$

Now, at $x = \pi$

$y\left(\pi\right)sec\pi = - 2cos\pi + 3$

$⇒ y\left(\pi\right)\left(- 1\right) = - 2\left(- 1\right) + 3$

$⇒ y\left(\pi\right) = - 5 .$

34965.text: Let $x = 9$ be a directrix of an ellipse $E$, whose centre is at the origin and eccentricity is $\dfrac{1}{3}$. Let $P(\alpha, 0)$, $\alpha > 0$, be a focus of $E$ and $AB$ be a chord passing through $P$. Then the locus of the mid point of $AB$ is :
34965.sol:
Given the directrix of the ellipse is $x = \dfrac{a}{e} = 9$ and eccentricity $e = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

$\dfrac{a}{1/3} = 9 \Rightarrow a = 3$

The value of $b^2$ is given by $b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2) = 9\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{9}\right) = 8$.

The equation of the ellipse is $\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{8} = 1$.

The focus $P(\alpha, 0)$ for $\alpha > 0$ is at $(ae, 0) = \left(3 \times \dfrac{1}{3}, 0\right) = (1, 0)$.

Let the midpoint of the chord $AB$ be $(h, k)$. The equation of the chord in terms of its midpoint is given by $T = S_1$ :

$\dfrac{hx}{9} + \dfrac{ky}{8} = \dfrac{h^2}{9} + \dfrac{k^2}{8}$

Since the chord passes through the focus $P(1, 0)$, substituting $x = 1$ and $y = 0$ gives:

$\dfrac{h}{9} = \dfrac{h^2}{9} + \dfrac{k^2}{8}$

$\dfrac{k^2}{8} = \dfrac{h}{9} - \dfrac{h^2}{9}$

$9k^2 = 8h(1 - h)$

Replacing $(h, k)$ with $(x, y)$, the locus of the midpoint is:

$9y^2 = 8x(1 - x)$

Answer: $9y^2 = 8x(1-x)$

35037.text: Let $L$ be a common tangent line to the curves $4{x}^{2} + 9{y}^{2} = 36$ and ${\left(2x\right)}^{2} + {\left(2y\right)}^{2} = 31$. Then the square of the slope of the line $L$ is ______.<gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
35037.sol:
Given curves are $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4} = 1$

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = \dfrac{31}{4}$

let slope of common tangent be $m$

so tangents are $y = mx \pm \sqrt{9{m}^{2} + 4}$

$y = mx \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{31}}{2}\sqrt{1 + {m}^{2}}$

hence $9{m}^{2} + 4 = \dfrac{31}{4}\left(1 + {m}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ 36{m}^{2} + 16 = 31 + 31{m}^{2} ⇒ {m}^{2} = 3$

35635.text: The number of solutions of the equation $\sin^{- 1}\left[{x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right] + \cos^{- 1}\left[{x}^{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right] = {x}^{2}$ for $x \in [ - 1, 1 ]$, and $[ x ]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x,$ is :<gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
35635.sol:
Given equation is

$\sin^{- 1}\left[{x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right] + \cos^{- 1}\left[{x}^{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right] = {x}^{2}$

Now, $\sin^{- 1}\left[{x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right]$ is defined if $- 1 \le \left[{x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right] \le 1$

$⇒ - 1 \le {x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} < 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 4}{3} \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ 0 \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{5}{3} . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, and $\cos^{- 1}\left[{x}^{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right]$ is defined if $- 1 \le \left[{x}^{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right] \le 1$

$⇒ - 1 \le {x}^{2} - \dfrac{2}{3} < 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{3} \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{8}{3}$

$⇒ 0 \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{8}{3} . . . \left(2\right)$

So, from $( 1 )$ and $( 2 )$ we can conclude $0 \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{5}{3}$

Case -$I:$ If $0 \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1} ( 0 ) + \cos^{- 1} ( - 1 ) = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ 0 + \pi = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} = \pi$ but $\pi \notin \left[0, \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

$⇒$ No value of $' x '$

Case - $II:$ If $\dfrac{2}{3} \le {x}^{2} < \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1} ( 1 ) + \cos^{- 1} ( 0 ) = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} = \pi$ but $\pi \notin \left[\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

$⇒$ No value of $' x '$

So, number of solutions of the equation is zero.

35759.text: Let $\left[t\right]$ denote the greatest integer $\le t$. If $\lambdaεR - \left\{0, 1\right\}, \lim_{x \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - x + \left|x\right|}{\lambda - x + \left[x\right]}\right| = L$, then $L$ is equal to
35759.sol:
$\lim_{x \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - x + \left|x\right|}{\lambda - x + \left[x\right]}\right| = L$

Let's find left-hand and right-hand limit.

For left-hand limit

$x = 0 - h, x \to 0, h \to 0, h > 0$

$LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - \left(- h\right) + \left|- h\right|}{\lambda - \left(- h\right) + \left[- h\right]}\right|$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h - \left(- h\right)}{\lambda + h + \left[- h\right]}\right|$

Since $h > 0 ⇒ \left[- h\right] = - 1$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h + h}{\lambda + h - 1}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda - 1\right|}$

For right-hand limit

$x = 0 + h, x \to 0, h \to 0, h > 0$

$RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - h + \left|h\right|}{\lambda - h + \left[h\right]}\right|$

Since $h > 0 ⇒ \left[h\right] = 0$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h + h}{\lambda + h + 0}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda\right|}$

For existence of limit $LHL = RHL$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda - 1\right|} = \dfrac{1}{\left|\lambda\right|}$

Cross multiply and square both side.

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = {\left(\lambda - 1\right)}^{2} ⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = {\lambda}^{2} + 1 - 2\lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Limit $L = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2$

36143.text: If $A = \left[\begin{array}{ll}0 \\ 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$ , then which one of the following statements is not correct?
36143.sol:
$A = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

${A}^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 0 \\ 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$

${A}^{3} = \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 0 \\ 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}0 & 1 \\ - 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

${A}^{4} = \left[\begin{cases}0 & 1 \\ - 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Option $\left(1\right)$ ${A}^{3} + I = A\left({A}^{3} - I\right)$

$\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 \\ 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ - 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$

$\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$ = $\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$ .....Correct

Option $\left(2\right)$ ${A}^{4} - I = {A}^{2} + I$

$\left[\begin{cases}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{cases}\right]$ ....Correct

Option $\left(3\right)$ $\left[\begin{cases}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] \times \left[\begin{cases}- 2 & 0 \\ 0 & - 2\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}0 & 2 \\ - 2 & 0\end{cases}\right]$ .....Incorrect

Option $\left(4\right)$

${A}^{3} - I = A ( A - I )$

$\left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] \times \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$

......Correct.

36336.text: The letters of the word "UDAYPUR" are written in all possible ways with or without meaning and these words are arranged as in a dictionary. The rank of the word "UDAYPUR" is
36336.sol:
Letters of UDAYPUR: A, D, P, R, U, U, Y (U repeated twice).
Words starting with a letter before U: letters A, D, P, R each give $\frac{6!}{2!} = 360$ arrangements $\Rightarrow 4 \times 360 = 1440$.
Fix U at position 1. Remaining: A, D, P, R, U, Y (all distinct).
Words starting with UA: $5! = 120$.
Fix UD at positions 1-2. Remaining: A, P, R, U, Y. No letter before A, so fix UDA.
Remaining: P, R, U, Y. Letters before Y: P, R, U give $3 \times 3! = 18$.
Fix UDAY. Remaining: P, R, U. No letter before P, fix UDAYP.
Remaining: R, U. Letter before U: R gives $1! = 1$.
Fix UDAYPU, last letter R: the word itself.
Rank $= 1440 + 120 + 18 + 1 + 1 = 1580$.

37613.text: The mean of five observations is $5$ and their variance is $9.20 .$ If three of the given five observations are $1,3$ and $8,$ then a ratio of other two observations is
37613.sol:
Let, the two unknown terms are $x \text{ and } y .$

The mean is defined as $\mu = \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{N}$

$⇒ 5 = \dfrac{1 + 3 + 8 + x + y}{5}$

$⇒ 25 = 12 + x + y$

$⇒ x + y = 13 . . . \left(1\right)$

And, the variance is defined as ${\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {\left({x}_{i} - \mu\right)}^{2}}{N} = \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}^{2}}{N} - {\mu}^{2}$

$⇒ 9.2 = \dfrac{1 + 9 + 64 + {x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}{5} - 25$

$⇒ 34.2 \times 5 = 74 + {x}^{2} + {y}^{2}$

$⇒ 171 = 74 + {x}^{2} + {y}^{2}$

$⇒ 97 = {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

Put the value of $y$ from equation $\left(1\right)$ and put in $\left(2\right),$ to get

$97 = {x}^{2} + {\left(13 - x\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 97 = {x}^{2} + 169 - 26x + {x}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{x}^{2} - 26x + 72 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 13x + 36 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right)\left(x - 9\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 4$ or $x = 9$

And, $y = 9$ or $y = 4$ respectively.

Hence, the ratio of $x: y$ is $4: 9$ or $9: 4 .$

40740.text: In an experiment, a set of reading are obtained as follows - $1.24 \mathrm{~mm}, 1.25 \mathrm{~mm}, 1.23 \mathrm{~mm}$, 1.21 mm. The expected least count of the instrument used in recording these readings is $\_\_\_\_$ mm.
40740.sol:
Least count is the smallest division readable on an instrument scale.
Given readings are 1.24 mm, 1.25 mm, 1.23 mm, 1.21 mm, all expressed to two decimal places.
The precision of measurement shows differences as small as 0.01 mm (e.g., 1.25 - 1.24 = 0.01 mm).
This indicates all readings can be recorded to the nearest 0.01 mm, which represents the smallest measurable division.
Therefore, the least count of the instrument is 0.01 mm.

44864.text: Which of the following amino acids is not optically active?

A compound shows optical activity, when a chiral carbon or asymmetrical carbon (ie, carbon which attached to four different groups or atoms) is present. Because chiral carbon is absent in glycine. So, it does not show optical activity. Other amino acids contain at least single asymmetric carbon atoms, so they show optical activity, eg, valine, leucine and isoleucine.

45209.subject: Botany
45209.text: During which stage in the complete oxidation of glucose are the greatest number of ATP molecules formed from ADP?
options: Conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl Co-A
45209.sol:
In glycolysis 4 ATP and $2 \mathrm{NADH}_2$ molecules are formed. These $2 \mathrm{NADH}_2$ molecules go to electron transport chain.
In oxidative decarboxylation no ATP molecule is formed but two molecules of $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ are formed from two molecules of pyruvate. These two $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ go to electron transport chain. In Krebs cycle 2 ATP, $6 \mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $2 \mathrm{FADH}_2$ molecules are formed from two molecule of acetyl Co-A. These $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $\mathrm{FADH}_2$ go to electron transport chain. In electron transport chain all $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $\mathrm{FADH}_2$ pass to electron carriers and yield 3 ATP and 2 ATP molecules per $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $\mathrm{FADH}_2$ respectively.
Thus,
4 ATP are formed in glycolysis
2 ATP in Krebs cycle and
34 ATP from electron transport chain
40 ATP
2 ATP molecules are used during glycolysis.
So, net gain of ATP molecules during one complete oxidation of a glucose molecule is 38 ATP.

& \Rightarrow \\

& \Rightarrow \quad 2-\sqrt{6} < x < 2+\sqrt{6} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2-2.449 < x < 2+2.449 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad-0.449 < x < 4.449

Expression can be written as $=(1+i)^{n_1}+(1-i)^{n_1}+(1+i)^{n_2}+(1-i)^{n_2}=2^{n_1 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_1}+2^{n_1 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_1}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_2}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_2}=2^{n_1 / 2}\left\{\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_1}+\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_1}\right\}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left\{\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_2}+\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_2}\right\}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left\{\cos \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}\right.\left.+\cos \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}-\sin \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}\right\}=2^{n_1 / 2} \cdot 2 \cos \frac{n_1 \pi}{4}+2^{n_2 / 2} \cdot 2 \cos \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}=\mathrm{real}$
ie, $n_1, n_2$ are any two positive integers.

54499.subject: Physics
54499.text: Two steel wires having same length are suspended from a ceiling under the same load. If the ratio of their energy stored per unit volume is $1: 4$, then the ratio of their diameters is found to be $\sqrt{k}: 1$. Find the value of $k$.
54499.sol:
Elastic potential energy stored in a loaded'wire,
$U=\frac{1}{2} \times($ Stress $\times$ Strain $\times$ Volume $) \therefore$ Energy stored per unit volume,
$U=\frac{U}{\text{ Volume }}=\frac{1}{2} \times$ Stress $\times$ Strain $=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{F}{A}\right)^2 \times \frac{1}{Y} \frac{U_A}{U_B}=\frac{\frac{1}{2 Y} \cdot \frac{F^2}{A_A^2}}{\frac{1}{2 Y} \cdot \frac{F^2}{A_B^2}}=\frac{A_B^2}{A_A^2}, \frac{U_A}{U_B}=\frac{d_B^4}{d_A^4}$
Here,$\frac{U_A}{U_B}=\frac{1}{4}, \frac{d_B^4}{d_A^4}=\frac{1}{4}$ or $\frac{d_B}{d_A}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \frac{d_A}{d_B}=\sqrt{2}: 1=\sqrt{k}: 1$ (given)
$\therefore \quad k=2$

55779.text: Which of the following is correct decreasing order of bond length regarding $\mathrm{N}_2, \mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ ?
55779.sol:
Bond lengths decrease with increasing bond multiplicity and increase with larger atomic radii. The bond order and atomic size determine the bond length: $\mathrm{N}_2$ has a triple bond, $\mathrm{O}_2$ a double bond, and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ a single bond.

$\mathrm{N}_2$: $\mathrm{N} \equiv \mathrm{N}$, bond length $\approx 109.8 pm
\mathrm{O}_2$: $\mathrm{O} = \mathrm{O}$, bond length $\approx 121 pm
\mathrm{Cl}_2$: $\mathrm{Cl} - \mathrm{Cl}$, bond length $\approx 199 pm

Since higher bond order corresponds to shorter bonds, and chlorine has the largest atomic radius, the order is \mathrm{Cl}_2 > \mathrm{O}_2 > \mathrm{N}_2$.

56806.subject: Chemistry
56806.text: What is number of moles of electron passed when a current of $2$ Amp flows through solution of electrolyte for $10$ minutes?
56806.sol:
Given, current $I = 2$ A and time $t = 10$ minutes $= 10 \times 60 = 600$ s.

Total charge passed is given by $Q = I \times t$

$Q = 2 \times 600 = 1200$ C

The charge of one mole of electrons is $1$ Faraday ($F \approx 96500$ C).

Number of moles of electrons $= \dfrac{Q}{F}$

Number of moles of electrons $= \dfrac{1200}{96500} = 0.012435$ mol

Number of moles of electrons $\approx 1.243 \times 10^{-2}$ mol

Answer: $1.243 \times 10^{-2}$

57588.text: Wurtz reaction is NOT possible with
57588.sol:
Wurtz reaction is used for the preparation of higher alkanes from alkyl halides using sodium metal in dry ether.

Primary and secondary alkyl halides readily undergo Wurtz reaction to form alkanes.

Tertiary alkyl halides, due to high steric hindrance, undergo dehydrohalogenation (elimination) rather than coupling when treated with sodium in dry ether, resulting in the formation of alkenes instead of alkanes.

Among the given options, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$ is a tertiary alkyl halide, so it does not undergo Wurtz reaction.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$

Ammonium acetate is a salt of a weak acid (acetic acid) and a weak base (ammonium hydroxide).

Sodium acetate is a salt of a weak acid (acetic acid) and a strong base (sodium hydroxide).

Copper (II) chloride is a salt of a strong acid (hydrochloric acid) and a weak base (copper (II) hydroxide).

Sodium carbonate is a salt of a weak acid (carbonic acid) and a strong base (sodium hydroxide).

Thus, copper (II) chloride is the correct example of a salt of a strong acid and a weak base.

Answer: Copper (II) chloride.

59946.subject: Chemistry
59946.text: Calculate the enthalpy of vaporisation of ethanol if 11.5 g of ethanol is completely vaporised by supplying 11.8 kJ of heat.
59946.sol:
The enthalpy of vaporization $\Delta H_{vap}$ represents the heat required to vaporize one mole of ethanol. Given that $11.8\text{ kJ}$ vaporizes $11.5\text{ g}$ of ethanol, we first determine the molar mass of ethanol as $C_2H_5OH$.

The molar mass is $2 \times 12.01 + 6 \times 1.008 + 16.00 = 46.068\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles vaporized is $\frac{11.5}{46.068} \approx 0.2496\text{ mol}$.

The enthalpy of vaporization is thus $\Delta H_{vap} = \frac{11.8}{0.2496} \approx 47.275\text{ kJ/mol}$, which rounds to $47.2\text{ kJ/mol}$.

60224.subject: Mathematics
60224.text: The value of $k$ such that the function $f(x) = \sin x - \cos x - kx + b$ is strictly decreasing for all real $x$ is
60224.sol:
Given $f(x) = \sin x - \cos x - kx + b$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \cos x + \sin x - k$

For $f(x)$ to be strictly decreasing for all real $x$, we must have $f'(x) \le 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ (with equality holding only at discrete points).

$\cos x + \sin x - k \le 0$

$k \ge \cos x + \sin x$

We know that the maximum value of $a \cos x + b \sin x$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}.

Maximum value of \cos x + \sin x = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$

Therefore, for the inequality to hold for all $x$, we must have:

$k \ge \sqrt{2}$

Among the given options, $k > \sqrt{2}$ satisfies this condition.

Answer: $k > \sqrt{2}$

60367.text: Let $\mathrm{P}(x)$ be a polynomial of degree 2 , with $\mathrm{P}(2)=-1, \mathrm{P}^{\prime}(2)=0, \mathrm{P}^{\prime \prime}(2)=2$, then $\mathrm{P}(1.001)$ is
60367.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Let } \mathrm{P}(x)=\mathrm{a} x^2+\mathrm{b} x+\mathrm{c} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}^{\prime}(x)=2 \mathrm{a} x+\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}^{\prime \prime}(x)=2 \mathrm{a} \\
& \mathrm{P}^{\prime \prime}(2)=2 \mathrm{a} \\
& \Rightarrow 2=2 \mathrm{a} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=1 \\
& \mathrm{P}^{\prime}(2)=2 \mathrm{a}(2)+\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow 0=4 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow 0=4(1)+\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=-4 \\
& \mathrm{P}(2)=\mathrm{a}(2)^2+\mathrm{b}(2)+\mathrm{c} \\
& \Rightarrow-1=4 \mathrm{a}+2 \mathrm{ b}+\mathrm{c} \\
& \Rightarrow-1=4(1)+2(-4)+\mathrm{c} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=3 \\
& \mathrm{P}(x)=x^2-4 x+3 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}^{\prime}(x)=2 x-4 \\
& x=1.001=1+0.001=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{h}
\end{aligned}$
Here, $\mathrm{a}=1, \mathrm{ h}=0.001\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{a})=\mathrm{P}(1)=1-4+3=0 \\
\mathrm{P}^{\prime}(\mathrm{a})=\mathrm{P}^{\prime}(1)=2-4=-2
\end{gathered}\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}(1.001)=0+(0.001)(-2)=-0.002$

61796.text: If $y=[(x+1)(2 x+1)(3 x+1) \ldots \ldots(\mathrm{n} x+1)]^{\frac{3}{2}}$, then $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}$ at $x=0$ is

$y=[(x+1)(2 x+1)(3 x+1) \ldots(\mathrm{n} x+1)]^{\frac{3}{2}}$
Taking 'log' on both sides, we get
 \begin{array}{r}
$\log y=$$\frac{3}{2}$[$\log$(x+1)+$\log$(2 x+1)+$\log$(3 x+1) \\
+\ldots+$\log$(n x+1)]
\end{array}$
Differentiating w.r.t. $ x$, we get

& \therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=\frac{3 y}{2} \left[\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{2}{2 x+1}+\frac{3}{3 x+1}+\ldots+\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{n} x+1}\right]\\
& \text{ Now at }x=0, y=[\underbrace{(1)(1)(1) \ldots(1)}_{ \mathrm{n} \text{ times }}]^{\frac{3}{2}}=1

62974.text: The logical statement $[\sim(\sim \mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q}) \vee(\mathrm{p} \wedge \mathrm{r}) \wedge(\sim \mathrm{q} \wedge \mathrm{r})]$ is equivalent to
62974.sol:
The given statement is $[\sim(\sim p \lor q) \lor (p \land r)] \land (\sim q \land r)$.

Applying De Morgan's law to $\sim(\sim p \lor q)$ yields $p \land \sim q$.

Substituting gives $[(p \land \sim q) \lor (p \land r)] \land (\sim q \land r)$.

The distributive law simplifies the disjunction to $p \land (\sim q \lor r)$.

The expression becomes $p \land (\sim q \lor r) \land (\sim q \land r)$.

Since $(\sim q \land r) \land (\sim q \lor r) \equiv \sim q \land r$, the entire expression reduces to $p \land \sim q \land r$.

This matches option A: $(p \land r) \land \sim q$.

63602.text: Three numbers are chosen at random from numbers 1 to 20. The probability that they are consecutive is
63602.sol:
The sample space consists of all 3-element subsets of $S = \{1, 2, \dots, 20\}$, yielding $\binom{20}{3} = \frac{20 \times 19 \times 18}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 1140$ equally likely outcomes.

Consecutive triplets correspond to sets of the form $\{x, x+1, x+2\}$ where $1 \leq x \leq 18$. There are 18 such sets, as the smallest starting value is 1 and the largest is 18.

The probability is thus $\frac{18}{1140} = \frac{3}{190}$, matching option C.

64835.subject: Mathematics
64835.sol:
The equation $\tan (\pi \cos \theta) = \cot (\pi \sin \theta)$ is solved by rewriting $\cot x = \tan \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)$, giving $\tan (\pi \cos \theta) = \tan \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \pi \sin \theta\right)$.

Applying the general solution for $\tan A = \tan B$ as $A = n\pi + B$ for integer $n$, we have $\pi \cos \theta = n\pi + \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \pi \sin \theta\right)$. Dividing by $\pi$ and rearranging yields $\cos \theta + \sin \theta = n + \frac{1}{2}$.

Since the range of $\cos \theta + \sin \theta$ is $[-\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}]$, it follows that $-\sqrt{2} \leq n + \frac{1}{2} \leq \sqrt{2}$. Solving the inequality gives $-1.914 \leq n \leq 0.914$, so the integer solutions are $n = -1$ and $n = 0$.

This implies $\cos \theta + \sin \theta = -\frac{1}{2}$ for $n = -1$, and $\frac{1}{2}$ for $n = 0$.

Using the identity $\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} (\cos \theta + \sin \theta)$, we find $\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right) = -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ or $\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$.

The value $\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ corresponds to option D.

66752.subject: Physics
66752.text: Magnetic flux linked with the coil in weber is given by the equation $\Phi = 5t^2 + 6t + 11$. The e.m.f. induced in the coil in the $5^{\text{th}}$ second will be
66752.sol:
The magnetic flux is given by $\Phi = 5t^2 + 6t + 11$.

The e.m.f. induced in the $5^{\text{th}}$ second is the average e.m.f. from $t = 4$ s to $t = 5$ s.

The magnitude of the average induced e.m.f. is $e = \dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{\Phi(5) - \Phi(4)}{5 - 4}$.

$\Phi(5) = 5(5)^2 + 6(5) + 11 = 125 + 30 + 11 = 166$ Wb

$\Phi(4) = 5(4)^2 + 6(4) + 11 = 80 + 24 + 11 = 115$ Wb

$e = \dfrac{166 - 115}{1} = 51$ V

Answer: $51$ V

66816.subject: Physics
66816.text: The current flowing through an inductor of self-inductance L is continuously increasing at constant rate. The variation of induced e.m.f. (e) verses $\mathrm{dI} / \mathrm{dt}$ is shown graphically by figure
66816.sol:
The induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) in an inductor is given by Faraday's law:

$e = -L \frac{dI}{dt}$

where $L$ is the self-inductance (a positive constant) and $\frac{dI}{dt}$ is the rate of change of current.

The equation indicates a linear relationship where the e.m.f. is proportional to the rate of current change.
The negative sign reflects Lenz's law: the induced e.m.f. opposes changes in current.
When $\frac{dI}{dt} > 0$, the e.m.f. is negative; when $\frac{dI}{dt} < 0$, the e.m.f. is positive.

The graph of $e$ versus $\frac{dI}{dt}$ must be a straight line through the origin with negative slope $-L$.

Analysis of the options:
Option A shows constant negative e.m.f. for positive $\frac{dI}{dt}$, inconsistent with proportionality.
Option B displays the correct linear relationship through the origin with negative slope.
Option C shows a nonlinear relationship, which is incorrect.
Option D has positive slope, contradicting Lenz's law.

Thus, graph B correctly represents $e = -L \frac{dI}{dt}$.

The correct choice is $\boxed{B}$.

67270.text: A body (mass $\mathrm{m}$ ) starts its motion from rest from a point distant $R_0  \left(R_0 > R\right)$ from the centre of the earth. The velocity acquired by the body when it reaches the surface of earth will be ($\mathrm{G}= universal constant of gravitation, \mathrm{M}=$ mass of earth, $\mathrm{R} = radius of earth)$
67270.sol:
According to law of conservation of energy,
$\begin{aligned}
& \quad \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=-\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}_0}-\left(\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)=\mathrm{GMm}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_0}\right) \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{v}^2=2 \mathrm{GM}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_0}\right)
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ The velocity acquired by the body when it reaches the surface of earth is:
$\mathrm{V}=\left[2 \mathrm{GM}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_0}\right)\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}$

67400.text: Energy of a gas/litre is $600$ joule, then what will be its pressure?
67400.sol:
The translational kinetic energy of an ideal gas is given by $E = \dfrac{3}{2}PV$

Rearranging for pressure, we get $P = \dfrac{2E}{3V}$

Given $E = 600$ J and $V = 1$ litre $= 10^{-3}$ m$^3$

Substituting the values:

$P = \dfrac{2 \times 600}{3 \times 10^{-3}}$

$P = 400 \times 10^3 = 4 \times 10^5$ N/m$^2$

Answer: $4 \times 10^5$ N/m$^2$

67985.subject: Physics
67985.text: Nickel shows ferromagnetic property at room temperature. If the temperature is increased beyond Curie temperature, then it will show
67985.sol: Nickel exhibits ferromagnetism because of a quantum physical effect called exchange coupling in which the electron spins of one atom interact with those of neighbouring atoms. The result is alignment of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms, inspite of the randomizing tendency of atomic collisions. This persistent alignment is what gives ferromagnetic materials their permanent magnetism. If the temperature of a ferromagnetic material is raised above a certain critical value, called the Curie temperature, the exchange coupling ceases to be effective. Most such materials then become simply paramagnetic; that is, the dipoles still tend to align with an external field but much more weakly, and thermal agitation can now more easily disrupt the alignment.

68114.text: A liquid is at rest in a container. In a sphere of influence, the liquid molecule at its centre is
options: attracted by other molecules in the sphere of influence.
attracted by other molecules outside sphere of influence.
repelled by other molecules outside the sphere of influence.
repelled by other molecules in the sphere of influence.
68114.sol:
The sphere of influence is an imaginary sphere drawn with a molecule as its centre and the intermolecular range as its radius.

The intermolecular force is attractive in nature for the molecules within this range.

Therefore, the liquid molecule at the centre of the sphere of influence is attracted by other molecules present inside the sphere of influence.

Molecules outside the sphere of influence are at a distance greater than the intermolecular range, so they do not exert any significant force on the central molecule.

Answer: attracted by other molecules in the sphere of influence.

68715.text: Two simple harmonic motions of angular frequency $300 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ and $3000 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ have same amplitude. The ratio of their maximum accelerations is
68715.sol:
Maximum acceleration in simple harmonic motion is given by $a_{\text\max} = A\omega^2$, where $A$ is the amplitude and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

Given identical amplitudes $A_1 = A_2 = A$ and angular frequencies $\omega_1 = 300 \text{ rad/s}$, $\omega_2 = 3000 \text{ rad/s}$, the ratio of maximum accelerations is:

This corresponds to ratio $1:10^2$, making option B correct.

69427.text: In a transistor amplifier, a change of 0.2 mA in the base current causes a change of 5 mA in the collector current. If input resistance is $2\ \text{k}\Omega$ and voltage gain is 75, the load resistance used in the circuit is
69427.sol:
The AC current gain $\beta$ is given by the ratio of the change in collector current to the change in base current:

$\beta = \dfrac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_B}$

Substituting the given values:

$\beta = \dfrac{5\ \text{mA}}{0.2\ \text{mA}} = 25$

The voltage gain $A_v$ of a transistor amplifier is given by:

$A_v = \beta \times \dfrac{R_L}{R_{in}}$

Substituting the known values into the formula:

$75 = 25 \times \dfrac{R_L}{2\ \text{k}\Omega}$

$\dfrac{R_L}{2\ \text{k}\Omega} = \dfrac{75}{25} = 3$

$R_L = 3 \times 2\ \text{k}\Omega = 6\ \text{k}\Omega$

Answer: $6\ \text{k}\Omega$

69947.subject: Physics
69947.text: A sample of an ideal gas $\left(\gamma=\frac{5}{3}\right)$ is heated at constant pressure. If 100J of heat is supplied to the gas , the work done by the gas is
69947.sol:
Applying the First Law of Thermodynamics for an ideal gas under constant pressure where heat $Q = 100 \text{ J}$ is supplied and the adiabatic index is $\gamma = \frac{5}{3}$.

The first law states $Q = \Delta U + W$, with $\Delta U$ representing the internal energy change and $W$ the work done. For an ideal gas, $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$ and $W = n R \Delta T$ at constant pressure.

Expressing $\Delta U$ in terms of $W$ gives $\Delta U = C_v (W / R)$. Using $C_v = R / (\gamma - 1)$ from the relation $\gamma = C_p / C_v$ and $C_p - C_v = R$, then $\Delta U = W / (\gamma - 1)$.

Substituting into the first law: $Q = W / (\gamma - 1) + W = W [1 / (\gamma - 1) + 1] = W (\gamma / (\gamma - 1))$.

Solving for $W$ yields $W = Q (\gamma - 1) / \gamma$. With $Q = 100 \text{ J}$ and $\gamma = 5/3$, $W = 100 (2/3) / (5/3) = 100 \times (2/5) = 40 \text{ J}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{40 \text{ J}}$

71321.subject: Biology
71321.text: In which phase of plant growth, the rate of growth slows down and comes to a steady state?
71321.sol:
The period of plant growth is generally divided into three phases: meristematic (cell division), elongation (cell enlargement), and maturation.

During the phase of cell division, cells are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei.

During the phase of cell elongation, there is increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition, leading to a rapid increase in size.

During the phase of cell maturation, cells attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications. In this phase, the rate of growth slows down and eventually comes to a steady state.

Answer: Phase of cell maturation.

71696.subject: Chemistry
71696.text: Identify the correct decreasing order of lattice enthalpy for metal fluorides from following.
71696.sol:
Lattice enthalpy is directly proportional to the product of charges of the ions and inversely proportional to the internuclear distance between them.

$U \propto \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r_+ + r_-}$

For alkali metal fluorides, the charges on the ions are the same (+1 and -1). The ionic radius of alkali metal cations increases down the group in the order: $\text{Li}^+ < \text{Na}^+ < \text{K}^+$.

As the size of the cation increases, the internuclear distance increases, which leads to a decrease in the lattice enthalpy.

Therefore, the decreasing order of lattice enthalpy is $\text{LiF} > \text{NaF} > \text{KF}$.

Answer: $\text{LiF} > \text{NaF} > \text{KF}$

71906.subject: Chemistry
71906.text: A sol gel process is based on
71906.sol:
The sol-gel process is a method for producing solid materials from small molecules.

The process involves the conversion of monomers into a colloidal solution (sol) that acts as the precursor for an integrated network (or gel) of either discrete particles or network polymers.

Typical precursors are metal alkoxides and metal chlorides, which undergo hydrolysis and polycondensation reactions.

These reactions are essentially inorganic polymerization reactions, leading to the formation of a continuous inorganic network.

Thus, the sol-gel process is based on inorganic polymerization reactions.

Answer: inorganic polymerization reactions

72391.subject: Physics
72391.text: The components which are used in regulated power supply as rectifier, filter and voltage regulator are
options: p-n junction diodes, Zener diode and inductor
p-n junction diode, capacitor and Zener diode
72391.sol:
In a regulated power supply, the following components are used for specific functions:

1. Rectifier: A p-n junction diode is used to convert alternating current (AC) into pulsating direct current (DC).

2. Filter: A capacitor is connected in parallel to the load to smooth out the ripples from the pulsating DC, providing a steadier DC voltage.

3. Voltage Regulator: A Zener diode is used in reverse bias to maintain a constant output voltage across the load, regardless of variations in the input voltage or load current.

Thus, the components used as a rectifier, filter, and voltage regulator are a p-n junction diode, a capacitor, and a Zener diode, respectively.

Answer: p-n junction diode, capacitor and Zener diode

Sentence Q continues the chronological progression, mentioning its ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries and introducing the people who kept its memory alive.

Thus, the correct and coherent sequence is S P R Q.

73816.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: The molecules of soap are sodium or potassium salts of long chain fatty acids
The molecules of soap contain both hydrophobic and hydrophilic ends
Detergents are more effective than soaps in hard water
In micelles the ionic-end of the molecules is towards oil droplet while the other end faces outside
73816.sol:
Soap molecules are sodium or potassium salts of long chain fatty acids. They consist of two parts: a hydrophobic (water-repelling) hydrocarbon tail and a hydrophilic (water-attracting) ionic head.

In a micelle formed around an oil droplet, the hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails point inwards and dissolve in the oil droplet, while the hydrophilic ionic ends point outwards and interact with the surrounding water.

Therefore, the statement that the ionic end is towards the oil droplet and the other end faces outside is incorrect.

Detergents are more effective than soaps in hard water because they do not form insoluble precipitates (scum) with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water.

Answer: In micelles the ionic-end of the molecules is towards oil droplet while the other end faces outside

77986.subject: Mathematics
77986.text: If $P(A) = 0.3$, $P(B) = 0.4$ and $P(A|B) = 0.5$, then what is the value of $P(B|A)$?
77986.sol:
Given $P(A) = 0.3$, $P(B) = 0.4$ and $P(A|B) = 0.5$.

Using the formula for conditional probability:

$P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$

$0.5 = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{0.4}$

$P(A \cap B) = 0.5 \times 0.4 = 0.2$

Now, finding $P(B|A)$:

$P(B|A) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)}$

$P(B|A) = \dfrac{0.2}{0.3} = \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.667$

Answer: $0.667$

79404.subject: Botany
79404.text: Vascular tissues in flowering plants develop from
79404.sol:
Histogen theory for shoot apical meristem has been proposed by Hanstein (1870). It advocates that there are three distinct meristematic zones (layers) called dermatogen periblem and plerome. The dermatogen is the outermost histogen giving rise to epidermis, periblem is the middle one producing the cortex and plerome is the innermost resulting in central cylinder (ie, vascular tissue).
Cork cambium (phellogen) is the secondary lateral meristem found in outer cortical region. Its cells divide periclinally cutting off cells towards the outside (forming cork or phellem) and inside (forming secondary cortex or phelloderm).

84038.subject: Zoology
84038.text: Nucleus of a donor embryonal cell/ somatic cell is transferred to an enucleated egg cell. Then, after the formation of organism what will be true?
options: Organism will have extranuclear genes of the donor cell.
Organism will have extra nuclear genes of the recipient cell.
Organism will have extra nuclear genes of both donor and recipient cells.
Organism will have nuclear genes of the recipient cell.
84038.sol:
The organism will have extranuclear genes of recipient cell. Since the recipient cell has already been enucleated (its nucleus is removed), the organism developing from it would have the nuclear genes of donor cell.
Related Theory
The egg cell is enucleated, so the organism will only have extranuclear genes from it. These genes are present in chloroplast and mitochondria and are transmitted along the cytoplasm. This results in cytoplasmic or maternal inheritance.

84113.subject: Zoology
84113.text: What are those structures that appear as 'beads-on-string' in the chromosomes when viewed under electron microscope?
84113.sol: Nucleosome is sub-microscopic sub-unit of chromatin which is formed by wrapping of DNA over a core of histone proteins. The term was coined by Oudet et. al, (1975). It is oblate structure with a length of $10 \mathrm{~nm}$ and a thickness of 5-5.7 nm. Its core is called nu-body. The latter is formed of four pairs of histone molecules- $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~A}$, $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~B}, \mathrm{H}_3$ and $\mathrm{H}_4$. DNA makes 1.75 turns over the octamer to form a nucleosome. Two adjacent nucleosomes are connected by a short segment of unbound DNA called linker DNA. A fifth type of histone called $\mathrm{H}_1$ is attached over the linker DNA. Nucleosomes appear as 'beads-on-string' in the chromosomes under electron microscope.

84120.text: What is true about RBCs in humans?

They transport about 80 per cent oxygen only and the rest 20 per cent of it is transported in dissolved state in blood plasma
They do not carry $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at all
84120.sol:
Nearly 20-25 per cent of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is transported by RBCs. It is caused by haemoglobin as carbamino haemoglobin. 70 per cent of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is carried as bicarbonates.
About 97 per cent of $\mathrm{O}_2$ is transported by RBCs in the blood. The remaining 3 per cent of $\mathrm{O}_2$ is carried in dissolved state through the plasma.

94134.subject: Physics
94134.text: A highly rigid cubical block $A$ of small mass $M$ and side $L$ is fixed rigidly on to another cubical block $B$ of the same dimensions and of low modulus of rigidity $η$ such that the lower face of $A$ completely covers the upper face of $B$. The lower face of $B$ is rigidly held on a horizontal surface. A small force $F$ is applied perpendicular to one of the side faces of $A$. After the force is withdrawn, block $A$ executes small oscillations, the time period of which is given by&
94134.sol:
Modulus of rigidity,$η = \dfrac{F}{A. \theta}$ Here, $A = L^{2}$

And

$\theta = \dfrac{\text{x}}{L}$

Therefore, restoring force is $F = - ηA\theta = - ηLx$



Or acceleration, $a = \dfrac{F}{M} = - \dfrac{ηL}{M} x$

Since, $a ∝ x$, oscillations are simaple harmonic in nature, time period of which is given by

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{| \dfrac{displacement}{acceleration} |} = 2\pi\sqrt{| \dfrac{x}{a} |} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{ηL}}$

94176.text: A thin prism of angle $5 °$ made of glass of refractive index ${μ}_{1} = 1. 5$ is combined with another prism of glass of refractive index ${μ}_{2} = 1. 75$. The combination of the prisms produces dispersion without deviation. The angle of the second prism should be

For dispersion without deviation

${\delta}_{1} + {\delta}_{2} = 0$

$\left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)A{⁡}_{1} + \left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)A{⁡}_{2} = 0$

$A{⁡}_{2} = - \dfrac{\left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)A{⁡}_{1}}{\left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)}$

Substituting the given values, we get

$A{⁡}_{2} = - \dfrac{\left(1 \cdot 5 - 1\right)5 °}{\left(1 \cdot 75 - 1\right)} = - \dfrac{10 °}{3}$

The negative sign shows that the two prisms must be joined in opposition.

94321.subject: Physics
94321.text: A thin uniform equilateral plate rests in a vertical plane with one of its vertex $A$ on a rough horizontal floor and another vertex $B$ on a smooth vertical wall. If the coefficient of friction $\mu = \dfrac{1}{3}$, then the least angle $\theta$ its base $AB$ can make with the horizontal surface is
94321.sol:
Let us assume that the side-length of the triangle is& $a$, then

$l = \dfrac{a}{3}$

${N}_{1} = Mg$

${f}_{1} = \mu{N}_{1} = {N}_{2}$

${N}_{2} = \muMg$

Balancing the torque about point $A$

$Mg \times lcos\left(30 ° + \theta\right) - {N}_{2} \times asin\theta = 0$

$⇒ Mg \times \dfrac{a}{3}cos\left(30 ° + \theta\right) - \muMg \times asin\theta = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}cos\theta - \dfrac{1}{2}sin\theta\right) = \musin\theta$

On solving further we get

$\theta = {cot}^{- 1} \left[2\mu + \dfrac{1}{3}\right]$

94682.subject: Physics
94682.text: A fixed mass of oxygen gas performs a cyclic process $ABCA$ as shown in the figure. Efficiency of the cycle will be
94682.sol:
$\text{A} \to \text{B}$ isochoric as $P$ is directly proportional to $T$

${\text{W}}_{\text{AB}} = 0$

${\text{Q}}_{\text{AB}} = \text{n} {\text{C}}_{\text{v}} \left(3 \text{T}   - \text{T}  \right)$

       $= \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right) \text{nR} 2 \text{T}   = 5 \text{nRT}  $

$B \to C$isothermal and thus $Q = W$ as there won't be any change in internal energy.
${\text{W}}_{\text{BC}} = \text{nR} 3 \text{T}   ln \left(\dfrac{{\text{P}}_{\text{B}}}{{\text{P}}_{\text{C}}}\right) = 3 \text{nRT}  \text{ln 3}$

       $= 3 \text{nRT}  \text{ln} 3 = {\text{Q}}_{\text{BC}}$

$C \to A$isobaric process
${\text{W}}_{\text{CA}} = \text{P} \left({\text{V}}_{\text{A}} - {\text{V}}_{\text{C}}\right) = \text{nR} \left({\text{T}}_{\text{A}} - 3 \text{T}  \right) = - 2 \text{n} \text{RT}  $

Efficiency of a cyclic process is given by

                  $η = \dfrac{\text{Work done in cyclic process}}{\text{Heat supplied to the system}} = \dfrac{\text{W}}{{\text{Q}}_{\text{in}}}$

Efficiency $η = \dfrac{3 {\text{nRT}}_{\text{A}} ln 3 - 2 {\text{nRT}}_{\text{A}}}{5 {\text{nRT}}_{\text{A}} + 3 {\text{nRT}}_{\text{A}} ln 3}$

                  $= \dfrac{\text{3 ln 3} - 2}{5 + 3 \text{ln 3}}$

96526.sol: The primary succession means the development of communities only on a newly exposed habitat with no record of earlier vegetation.& An important characteristic of all communities is that composition and structure constantly change in response to the changing environmental conditions. During ecological succession is a series of progressive changes in the species that make up a community is observed. This change is orderly and sequential, parallel with the changes in the physical environment. These changes lead finally to a community that is in near equilibrium with the environment.

98709.text: According to the Valence bond theory, which statement is incorrect regarding bonding between two carbon atoms?
options: A sigma(σ) bond is weaker than a $\text{\pi} - \text{b}\text{o}\text{n}\text{d}$
A sigma bond is stronger than a $\text{\pi} - \text{b}\text{o}\text{n}\text{d}$
A double bond is stronger than a single bond
A double bond is shorter than a single bond
98709.sol:
A $\text{\sigma} -$ bond is stronger than a $\text{\pi} -$ bond.
Sigma $\left(\text{\sigma}\right)$ bonds are formed by head-on overlap of unhybridised $\text{s} - \text{s}, \text{p} - \text{p}\text{o}\text{r}\text{s} - \text{p}$ orbitals and hybridized orbitals $\left(\text{s}\text{p}, \text{s}{\text{p}}^{2}, \text{s}{\text{p}}^{3}, \text{s}{\text{p}}^{3}\text{d}\text{a}\text{n}\text{d}\text{s}{\text{p}}^{3}{\text{d}}^{2}\right)$~. Hence,& $\text{\sigma}$ bond are strong bonds. Where as Pi $\left(\text{\pi}\right) -$ bonds are formed by side-wise overlap of unhybridised p and d orbitals. Hence $\text{\pi}$ bonds are weak bonds.

100192.text: In a system of units if force $(F)$, acceleration $(A)$, and time ( $T$ ) are taken as fundamental units, then the dimensional formula of energy is :
100192.sol:
Let energy $E=F^x A^y T^3$
Writing the dimensions on both sides
$\begin{aligned} & {\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{ T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]^x\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-2}\right]^y[\mathrm{ T}]^2} \\ & {\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{ T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{M}^x \mathrm{ L}^{x+y} \mathrm{ T}^{-2 x-2 y+z}\right]}\end{aligned}$
On comparing both sides
$\begin{aligned} & x=1 \\ & x+y=2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=2-x=2-1=1 \\ & \text{$ and $} \quad-2 x-2 y+z=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow-2 \times 1-2 \times 1+z=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad z=-2+2+2 \\ & =2 \\ & \end{aligned} \therefore$ Dimensional formula of energy
$=F A T^2$

100589.subject: Physics
100589.text:
Assertion : In the system of two blocks of equal masses as shown, the coefficient of friction between the blocks (\(\mu_2\)) is less than coefficient of friction (\(\mu_1\)) between lower block and ground.
For all values of force \(F\) applied on upper block lower block remains at rest.
Reason : Frictional force on lower block due to upper block is not sufficient to overcome the frictional force on lower block due to ground.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true
100589.sol:
Why assertion is true
- For two equal-mass blocks, the maximum static friction at the ground is \(\mu 1(2 \mathrm{mg})\), which exceeds any friction demand transmitted from the top block because \(\mu 2 < \mu 1\) limits the interface force first. Hence, the lower block can remain at rest for all applied F.
Why reason is correct
- The friction exerted by the upper block on the lower is bounded by \(\mu 2 \mathrm{mg}\), which is smaller than the maximum ground friction \(\mu 1(2 \mathrm{mg})\); therefore, this interface force can't overcome ground friction, keeping the lower block stationary.

Reason : Potential energy is defined only for conservative forces.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true
100805.sol:
Spring force follows Hooke's law \(F=-k x\).
Work done by spring depends only on initial and final positions, not the path \(\rightarrow\) so it is conservative.
For conservative forces, we can define a potential energy function (\(U=\frac{1}{2} k x^2\)).
Hence, spring force is conservative because potential energy is defined only for conservative forces.
100805.meta: Assertion: Spring force is a conservative force. Reason : Potential energy is defined only for conservative forces.

101179.subject: Physics
101179.text: A uniform circular disc has mass $M$ and radius $R$. Let $K_1$ be its radius of gyration about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane. Let $K_2$ be its radius of gyration about an axis tangential to its edge and lying in the plane of the disc. The ratio $K_1 : K_2$ is:
101179.sol:
The moment of inertia of the disc about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is:
$I_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} M R^2$
Since $I_1 = M K_1^2$, the radius of gyration $K_1$ is:
$K_1 = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$

The moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter is $I_d = \dfrac{1}{4} M R^2$.
Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a tangent in the plane of the disc is:
$I_2 = I_d + M R^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} M R^2 + M R^2 = \dfrac{5}{4} M R^2$
Since $I_2 = M K_2^2$, the radius of gyration $K_2$ is:
$K_2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2} R$

The ratio $K_1 : K_2$ is:
$\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{\sqrt{5} R}{2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{10}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}$

101185.subject: Physics
101185.text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a uniform solid sphere about an axis tangent to its surface to the radius of gyration of the sphere about its diameter is
101185.sol:
For a uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$:

Moment of inertia about its diameter is $I_{\text{diameter}} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.
Radius of gyration about the diameter, $k_{\text{diameter}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_{\text{diameter}}}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R$.

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a tangent is $I_{\text{tangent}} = I_{\text{diameter}} + MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2$.
Radius of gyration about the tangent, $k_{\text{tangent}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_{\text{tangent}}}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5}}R$.

The required ratio is $\dfrac{k_{\text{tangent}}}{k_{\text{diameter}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7/5}R}{\sqrt{2/5}R} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{7}:\sqrt{2}$

101711.subject: Physics
101711.text: A tiny spherical glass bead is projected vertically downwards into a deep column of highly viscous oil. Its initial downward velocity $v_0$ is twice its terminal velocity ($v_0 = 2v_t$). Which of the following descriptions correctly shows the variation of its velocity ($v$) with time ($t$)?
options: A curve starting at $v_0$ on the velocity axis and decreasing with a continuously flattening slope to approach a horizontal asymptote at $v_t$.
A curve starting at $v_0$ on the velocity axis and decreasing continuously to approach zero asymptotically.
A straight line starting at $v_0$ on the velocity axis and decreasing linearly until it abruptly becomes horizontal at $v_t$.
A curve starting at $v_0$ on the velocity axis and increasing with a continuously flattening slope to approach a higher horizontal asymptote.
101711.sol:
The net downward force on the spherical bead is given by $F_{net} = W_{eff} - F_v$, where $W_{eff}$ is the effective weight (weight minus buoyancy) and $F_v$ is the velocity-dependent viscous drag.

At terminal velocity $v_t$, the net force is zero, so $W_{eff} = 6\pi\eta r v_t$.

The bead is projected with an initial velocity $v_0 = 2v_t$. Since $v_0 > v_t$, the initial upward viscous drag is greater than the downward effective weight.

This results in a net upward force, causing the bead to decelerate. As the velocity decreases, the viscous drag decreases, and the net upward force (and thus the retardation) decreases.

The velocity will continuously decrease from $v_0$ and asymptotically approach the terminal velocity $v_t$ from above. The graph is a curve starting at $v_0$ and flattening out to a horizontal asymptote at $v_t$.

Answer: A curve starting at $v_0$ on the velocity axis and decreasing with a continuously flattening slope to approach a horizontal asymptote at $v_t$.

102137.subject: Physics
102137.text: A diatomic gas $(\gamma=1.4)$ does 200 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Find the heat given to the gas in the process.
102137.sol:
For a diatomic gas
$C_V=\frac{5}{2} R$ and $C_p=\frac{7}{2} R$
The work done in an isobaric process is
$\begin{aligned} W & =p\left(V_2-V_1\right)=n R\left(T_2-T_1\right) \\ \Rightarrow T_2-T_1 & =\frac{W}{n R}\end{aligned}$
The heat given in an isobaric process is
$\begin{aligned} Q & =n C_p\left(T_2-T_1\right) \\ n C_p \frac{W}{n R} & =\frac{7}{2} W \\ & =\frac{7}{2} \times 200 \mathrm{~J} \\ & =700 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
102137.meta: A diatomic gas (γ=1.4) does 200 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Find the heat given to the gas in the process.
